New site? Copy the [starter](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/tree/main/starter) instead -- it has the extension installed. This page is for adding the library to a site you already have.

mathviz ships two ways from one source tree. Both give you the same `window.VM`, the same CSS, and the same behaviour.

## Quarto site, book or document

```sh
quarto add apurvanakade/mathviz@v1.1.1
```

This copies the extension into `_extensions/apurvanakade/mathviz/` in your project. Enable it project-wide in `_quarto.yml`, or per page in front matter:

```yaml
filters:
  - mathviz
```

The filter puts the minified `mathviz.min.js` and `mathviz.min.css` (served from your own `site_libs/`) into every HTML page's `<head>`, and on every page with `{ojs}` cells, math.js and Plotly ahead of them (from a CDN, pinned to the versions the library is tested against). All three scripts are deferred, so none of them holds up the page's first paint, and they still run in order, before the first OJS cell.

### Options

All optional, under a `mathviz:` key in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
mathviz:
  plotly: false             # your pages draw with D3/canvas/Plot -- skip Plotly
  mathjs: false             # ...or math.js. Either also accepts true or a URL
  css: false                # bring your own stylesheet
  referrer: same-origin     # emit <meta name="referrer"> ahead of the CDN tags
```

| Key | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `plotly` | `"auto"` (default), `true`, `false`, or a URL | Whether to add the Plotly tag, and from where. `"auto"` adds it to pages with `{ojs}` cells only; `true` or a URL adds it to every page -- for a page that draws Plotly charts from its own `<script>` with no OJS (put that code in a `DOMContentLoaded` listener: the tag is deferred). With `false` the Plotly patch is a silent no-op and the `VM.plotting` theme functions still work for Observable Plot. |
| `mathjs` | `"auto"` (default), `true`, `false`, or a URL | The same, for math.js. `VM.expressions.*` take the instance as an argument, so a page that loads math.js another way passes that. |
| `css` | `true` (default) or `false` | Whether to add `mathviz.css`. With `false` you supply the `--vm-*` tokens and the `ojs-*` rules yourself -- see [Theming](theming.qmd). |
| `referrer` | a [referrer policy](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta/name/referrer) string | Emits `<meta name="referrer" content="…">` **before** the CDN tags, so the third-party origins don't see a page's path or query string -- which on a math page is the reader's own input. Visual Math Lab uses `same-origin`. |

### Options for one page {#page-options}

To change an option on one page, use `mathviz-page:` in that page's front matter, **never `mathviz:`**:

```yaml
---
title: "Gallery"
mathviz-page:
  category-cloud: true
---
```

The page gets every option from `_quarto.yml`, with its own `mathviz-page:` keys on top. A key there replaces the project's value for that key; a map such as `share:` is replaced whole, not merged.

A `mathviz:` block in a page's front matter doesn't add to the project's; it replaces it, so that page silently loses every option `_quarto.yml` sets: its referrer meta, fonts, sidebar search and the rest. Nothing warns you and the page still renders. [Internals](reference/internals.qmd#the-lua-filters-odd-shape) explains why.

Further keys turn on self-hosted fonts and site-wide chrome (a sidebar search box, a category cloud, embedding, a Share button, a Report bug popup), and the extension ships an optional Quarto theme. All are off by default -- see [Site extras](site.qmd).

### Versions and updating

```sh
quarto update apurvanakade/mathviz@v1.1.1    # move to a release
quarto add apurvanakade/mathviz@v1.1.1       # pin at install time
```

Always name the tag. Without one (or with `@latest`), Quarto installs the `main` branch, which can be ahead of the last release.

To stay on the latest release without thinking about it, run the [site kit](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/tree/main/kit)'s `update-mathviz.sh` as a `pre-render` hook. It updates the extension before each render -- within the major version you have, since only a new major may change what your pages call -- and keeps the installed copy when you're offline. When a new major is out it says so; render once with `MATHVIZ_UPGRADE=1` to take it.

## Any other web page

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/apurvanakade/mathviz@v1.1.1/dist/mathviz.min.css">
<script defer src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjs@15.2.0/lib/browser/math.js"></script>
<script defer src="https://cdn.plot.ly/plotly-2.35.2.min.js"></script>
<script defer src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/apurvanakade/mathviz@v1.1.1/dist/mathviz.min.js"></script>
```

- `mathviz.min.js`/`.min.css` are the minified bundle (a quarter of the size; a source map points devtools at the readable code). `dist/mathviz.js` and `dist/mathviz.css` are the same code with every comment, to read.
- Load **Plotly before `mathviz.min.js`**, and keep `defer` on all three or on none: deferred scripts run in document order, after the page has been parsed. If Plotly arrives later (a dynamic import), call [`VM.plotting.installPlotlyPatch()`](reference/plotting.qmd#installPlotlyPatch) yourself.
- Pin the tag in the URL. jsDelivr also serves `@main`, but a tag is what you can reason about.
- Without Quarto and Observable Inputs, some CSS has nothing to attach to; [Internals](reference/internals.qmd#host-markup) says what degrades and what doesn't.
